team.claim: Parker Conrad (b. 1980), co-founder and CEO of Rippling; previously co-founded Wikinvest/SigFig (co-CEO, left 2012) and Zenefits (CEO, resigned February 2016); started career as product manager at Amgen.
Prasanna Sankar co-founded Rippling in April 2016 and served as CTO; he was still co-founder/CTO in a March 2019 interview (current status in the company not confirmed in corpus).
Current executives include Adam Swiecicki, Chief Financial Officer (listed on Yahoo Finance and Crunchbase).
Charles (Matthew) MacInnis listed as COO and Bridget Abraham as Chief Compliance Officer on Crunchbase (aggregator data).
Founder history: in October 2017, without admitting or denying guilt, Conrad agreed to pay a fine to the SEC to settle charges of misleading investors about regulatory compliance at Zenefits.
No notable executive departures in the last two years were found in the corpus (see missing_fields).

output.company: Rippling (Rippling Inc., San Francisco-based workforce management software company)

funding.claim: Series A: $45M led by Kleiner Perkins (Mamoon Hamid), with Initialized Capital, Threshold Ventures (formerly DFJ Venture), and Y Combinator participating.
Series B: $145M led by Founders Fund.
Series C: $250M led by Sequoia Capital Global Equities and Global Growth, with Greenoaks and other existing investors participating (October 2021, $6.5B valuation per TacticalVC).
Series D: $250M co-led by Bedrock and Kleiner Perkins, with Y Combinator, Sequoia Capital and others; valued at $11.25 billion.
Series E: $500M led by Greenoaks at $11.25B valuation (same as Series D), closed in ~12 hours during the March 2023 SVB collapse to cover customer payrolls.

Series F: $200M in new financing plus agreements to repurchase up to $590M of equity from current employees, former employees and early investors; valued at $13.5 billion (blog updated Sep 5, 2024; Reuters reported the round as Coatue-led on April 22, 2024).

Series G: $450M in new financing plus repurchase of up to $200M of employee equity, valuing the company at $16.8 billion; investors include Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford, and Y Combinator (no lead investor per Sacra).
Total funding raised to $1.85 billion with the Series G; CNBC reported at the time that Rippling said an IPO was not imminent.

output.verdict: Rippling looks strong on fundamentals: ~$1B annualized revenue by March-July 2026 at ~78% growth (company claim, corroborated by Sacra's independent estimate), 20,000+ customers, a $16.8B Series G valuation (May 2025) with blue-chip investors, and a multi-product platform model showing ~200% net revenue retention. What needs a closer look: the unresolved RICO/espionage litigation with Deel (with some Deel counterclaims still live as of September 2026), reported sanctions-related scrutiny over Russia contractor payments, deteriorating Glassdoor sentiment (down 4% YoY, 34% CEO approval), and the absence of any audited or independently verified financials - every revenue figure traces to the company or an aggregator.

business.claim: Sells a unified cloud platform of over two dozen products across HR, IT, and Spend — including payroll, benefits, SSO/identity management, bill pay, and corporate cards — targeting businesses of all sizes.

Business model is B2B SaaS subscription priced per-employee-per-month by module, plus transactional revenue from currency exchange on international payroll, corporate card interchange, instant wage transfers, and Employer of Record services where Rippling is the legal employer.
Supports payroll and workforce management in 185+ countries, covering US and global entities on the same platform (company claim).
Geographies: headquartered in San Francisco with offices in California, Ireland (European HQ in Dublin), the UK, India (Bengaluru), and Australia (first APAC office in Sydney).
Founded by Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar (co-founded 2016, launched 2017) in San Francisco; privately owned; customers pay a monthly fee for access to the software platform.
Product expansion continues: launched Rippling AI, then in June 2026 launched Rippling Data Cloud, a business-intelligence product connecting organizational and third-party business data.

traction.claim: Customer count reached 20,000+ as of May 2025 (TechCrunch, May 9, 2025).

Company claim: ARR grew from $175M (2022) to $350M (end of 2023) to $570M (early 2025) to $1B+ (April 2026, Parker Conrad on X / SaaStr), ~78% YoY growth at the $1B milestone, with growth accelerating for three consecutive quarters heading into 2026.
Sacra estimate: Rippling hit $1B in annualized revenue in March 2026, up from $850M at end of 2025, growing 78% YoY (aggregator estimate, not company-reported).

Company claim: PEO segment customer retention of 99.5% during the Fall 2024 renewal season; 10+ product lines each generate over $1M ARR, with new products reaching $1M ARR within 5-6 months of launch.
Net revenue retention of approximately 200% as of May 2022 (Contrary Research estimate), vs 110-120% median for enterprise SaaS.
Partnership: Sigma360 and Rippling announced a partnership in June 2026 to power real-time sanctions screening across Rippling's global payments infrastructure (press release via stockanalysis.com).
Named customers on the company's enterprise site include Walker Advertising, Morning Consult, and Four Hands (company claim).

red_flags.claim: Prolonged, escalating litigation with closest competitor Deel (RICO/trade-secret espionage case since March 2025, Deel countersuit) creates ongoing management-distraction and discovery exposure; several Deel counterclaims against Rippling survived and are moving forward alongside those ordered to arbitration.
Reported scrutiny over facilitating payments to contractors in Russia amid sanctions, with potential banking-partner implications (Yahoo Finance profile claim, unverified against a regulator docket).

Employee-sentiment trend is deteriorating: Glassdoor overall rating down 4% over the last 12 months and only 34% CEO approval - notable given payroll/HR is the core product and service quality depends on people.
Still unprofitable as of 2024 (Reuters), with heavy reliance on primary financing plus employee-equity buybacks ($590M Series F, $200M Series G tender) rather than self-funding.
2023 SVB collapse froze Rippling's funds and briefly stopped customer payrolls - an operational-concentration incident showing systemic risk when the payroll layer for thousands of businesses fails.

Founder pattern: Parker Conrad's prior company Zenefits collapsed under a regulatory scandal and he settled SEC charges in 2017 - relevant governance-history context for diligence, though nothing comparable has occurred at Rippling itself.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor (aggregator): Rippling has an overall rating of 3.6/5 from 1,300+ employee reviews, a rating that has DECREASED 4% over the last 12 months; 66% would recommend working there, 75% have a positive outlook; work-life balance rated 3.0/5, culture and values 3.5, career opportunities 3.9.

Glassdoor (aggregator): only 34% of Rippling reviewers approve of the CEO; Customer Support employees rate the company 3.0/5 (20 reviews), 22% below the IT-industry average, with customer-support compensation rated 2.8/5.
Glassdoor (aggregator): compensation and benefits rated 3.9/5 and stable over the past 12 months.

Court dockets read directly (PACER/Irish courts); legal claims sourced from Bloomberg and company blog
Any regulatory enforcement action directly against Rippling (none found in sources checked)

financial_signals.claim: Sacra estimates $1B in annualized revenue as of March 2026, up from $850M at end of 2025, growing 78% YoY (aggregator estimate).
As of July 2026, Rippling's annual revenue was around $1 billion (Wikipedia, citing a 2026 TechCrunch interview with Parker Conrad) - company claim.
Headcount trend: ~2,800 employees (2024, Reuters), 5,000 (2025, Wikipedia infobox); Latka reports 5,000 employees as of November 2025, up from 3,630 a year earlier (aggregator data).
UnifyGTM observes 7,415 Rippling employee profiles in its July 2026 headcount snapshot - explicitly a profile-coverage measure, not a company-reported total (aggregator data).
Profitability: as of 2024 the company remained unprofitable while holding $1 billion in cash for expansion (Reuters, via Wikipedia).
Blind discussions (social, unverified) reference Rippling layoffs starting around August-September 2022; no verified layoff numbers found in the corpus for 2022-2026.
Hiring signal: company blog states it is 'hiring across all roles' as of the May 2025 Series G announcement.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: In March 2025, Rippling sued competitor Deel in Ireland alleging corporate espionage; shortly afterwards Deel countersued and filed an anti-SLAPP motion in Delaware.

Company claim: a federal judge (Judge Breyer, N.D. Cal.) issued a 49-page ruling on Feb 25, 2026 allowing Rippling's civil RICO and trade secret theft lawsuit against Deel, its CEO, COO and Board Chair to proceed toward trial in California, rejecting Deel's forum and dismissal efforts; the court found three plausible predicate acts (obstruction of justice, wire fraud, theft of trade secrets).

Bloomberg (Sept 26, 2026): federal judge rejected Deel's bid to strike testimony by a central witness, refused to reopen his decision letting Rippling's claims proceed, ordered Deel's most serious counterclaims into arbitration, and dismissed several of Deel's false-advertising claims while allowing others to move forward.
In April 2025, the alleged Deel spy admitted to espionage, in what Fortune called 'a major scandal rocking the HR world.'

Regulatory history of the founder: Conrad settled SEC charges (October 2017, fine paid, no admit/deny) over misleading investors about regulatory compliance at his prior company Zenefits - not a Rippling action.

Yahoo Finance profile flags that Rippling 'has faced scrutiny for facilitating payments to contractors in Russia amidst ongoing sanctions' and that continued banking-partner scrutiny could weigh on growth (secondary profile claim, no court/regulator docket found in corpus).

No data breach, regulatory enforcement action, or sanctions action directly against Rippling was found in the corpus; the March 2023 SVB collapse froze Rippling's funds and temporarily halted customer payrolls before ~$500M emergency funding was raised (operational, not legal, event).
